name: Fastbreak
label: Revelation
lede: Teenagers from Bethel, Connecticut who named their first album after a Jerky Boys prank call, moved to Boston, got called Fatbreak by Fat Wreck Chords, and burned out by 2000.

eras.title: Not old school, the only school
eras.text: Fastbreak started as middle-schoolers in Bethel, a suburb of Danbury, Connecticut, and grew up in the shadow of an older local band, Cornerstone, whose bassist was singer Patrick Rorick's brother. When Cornerstone ended, Fastbreak inherited its crowd, its motto and two of its members.

years.h: Fastbreak form in Bethel, Connecticut, average age 15
years.p: According to Revelation, the band starts as a four-piece with an average age of fifteen. Cornerstone's motto, Not Old School, The Only School, becomes their own.

years.h: Cornerstone breaks up and hands Fastbreak its crowd
years.p: Cornerstone, the older Connecticut band that had taken two Fastbreak members and featured Patrick Rorick's brother Kevin on bass, ends. Fastbreak pick up its momentum and local support.

years.h: "Hate Your Way" live in Simsbury CT, March 25, 1995
yt: "Hate Your Way" live in Simsbury CT, March 25, 1995

years.p: After the Youth Pride demo, Fastbreak put out two 7"s in 1996, on Third Party Records and Stand Hard Records, and catch on in New Jersey.

years.h: Neal St. Clair joins; Fastbreak tour west with Shutdown
years.p: Guitarist Neal St. Clair comes in, and a summer tour with New York's Shutdown takes Fastbreak out of New England for the first time.

eras.title: Fast cars, a prank call, and Boston
eras.text: Boston's Big Wheel Recreation made Fastbreak's first album and gave it art that pointedly didn't look youth crew. By the end of the year the band was moving to Boston, where Neal St. Clair and drummer Luke Garro were also playing in In My Eyes.

years.h: Fast Cars, Fast Women · Big Wheel Recreation
years.p: Recorded January to February 1998 with producer Dean Baltulonis, with art direction by Rama Mayo. The title comes from a Jerky Boys prank call.
years.xp:
Around this time Fat Wreck Chords turned the band down with a rejection letter addressed to Fatbreak, which Patrick Rorick and Neal St. Clair still laugh about.

Iodine Recordings later reissued the album, remastered, with demos and expanded packaging.

years.p: A summer 1998 tour with Boston's Ten Yard Fight takes the Connecticut band all the way to California.

years.h: Fastbreak move to Boston, in waves
years.p: Members relocate to Boston one by one. Neal St. Clair and Luke Garro are also in In My Eyes by then.

eras.title: Whenever you're ready, then done
eras.text: Revelation signed Fastbreak off a cassette, and the second album went more melodic and more personal, closer to Lifetime and later Gorilla Biscuits. It split the audience, and a long European tour broke the band's spirit.

years.h: Revelation signs Fastbreak off a Big Wheel cassette
years.p: Revelation A&R Jason Upright hears Fastbreak's demo tracks on a tape Big Wheel Recreation sent over. The label didn't tell them what to play, but pushed the band's image in ads, which Patrick Rorick later regretted.

years.src: No Echo · Revelation Records pressing history
years.p: Made on about a $5,000 budget, with [[Dag Nasty|4709dd69-1034-4634-9e88-d1099453b192]] and Lifetime in its melodies and Patrick Rorick's most inward lyrics. Revelation's first vinyl run: 226 on yellow.

years.h: Four weeks in Europe with [[Cause for Alarm|1940001f-3270-4d87-9501-eb243d5f9f50]]
years.p: Booked by M.A.D., the European tour runs over four weeks. Some shows land and others leave the band feeling isolated, and it takes a toll.
years.xp: Fastbreak also did six weeks in the US that summer with [[Farside|c6d7e9ab-e369-4dc2-b6a8-1fa7def9c069]] and [[Saves the Day|593f8594-83ad-4df4-a9b8-e4d225f55440]].

years.p: The new songs weren't connecting, and singing such personal material fed Patrick Rorick's anxiety and depression, he told No Echo. The whole band agreed to stop.
years.xp:
Rorick said he didn't want to think about demographics or crossing over. Drummer Luke Garro went on to [[Piebald|403bc4cd-602c-4b59-8379-05cb24f66aa6]], and bassist Don Raymond eventually played with [[The Format|81b07a2a-cdf0-4c5e-a68c-8d910e1f0ea6]]. Rorick turned to spiritual pursuits and stayed away for years.

Early guitarist Chris Legg, later of Break Faith, has since died.

eras.title: A guitar shop in Riverside
eras.text: Neal St. Clair's son Tate started his own hardcore band in Los Angeles, Start Today, and that pulled Fastbreak out of retirement for one unannounced set.

q: literally felt like a Fastbreak show from 1996
years.h: Unannounced Fastbreak set at a Riverside guitar shop
years.p: Three of Fastbreak's five, without Patrick Rorick and with Don Raymond flying in, open for [[Piebald|403bc4cd-602c-4b59-8379-05cb24f66aa6]] at a guitar shop in Riverside, California. Neal St. Clair said it felt like 1996.
